The `lic-dsf-2025-08-12` package is a Python reimplementation of the
IMF-World Bank Low-Income Country Debt Sustainability Framework (LIC-DSF)
IDA21 workbook, vintage 2025-08-12. Use it when you want the workbook's
mechanical results -- risk-rating signals, tailored-stress flags, fiscal-space
text, and the Chart Data series behind the DSA figures -- from a reproducible
script rather than from a live `.xlsm` file.

The package calculates the same published surface as the workbook's
`Chart Data` sheet. Display tabs such as `Output 2-1` and `Output 2-2` mostly
mirror that sheet. Yellow input cells on Inputs 1-8 remain the economist's
entry point; green engine sheets (`Macro-Debt_Data`, `PV_Base`, stress tabs)
are calculation surfaces, not a public API.

## Install

```bash
uv add lic-dsf-2025-08-12
```

The public functions live in `lic_dsf_2025_08_12.api`. Template labels,
projection years, and the snapshot of the IDA21 workbook sit in
`lic_dsf_2025_08_12.data`.

## A first result

Some Chart Data cells depend only on the country name. The natural-disaster
tailored test is one of them: the workbook stores a 0/1 applicability flag at
`Chart Data!I17`.

```{python}
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12.api import compute_tailored_stress_natural_disaster_applicable

compute_tailored_stress_natural_disaster_applicable(country="Bangladesh")
```

`1.0` means the test applies; `0.0` means it does not. Country names must
match the workbook spelling exactly -- `Bangladesh` works, `BGD` does not.

```{python}
compute_tailored_stress_natural_disaster_applicable(country="Ghana")
```

Ghana is a valid LIC-DSF country, but it is not on the natural-disaster list,
so the flag is `0.0`.

## Recommended route

1. Read how to [call `compute_*` functions](user-guide/calling-compute-functions.qmd)
   and how to load the template snapshot.
2. Map your country file onto the [Input 1-8 arguments](user-guide/country-inputs.qmd).
3. Evaluate the [risk-rating signals](user-guide/risk-ratings.qmd) you would
   quote in the DSA write-up.
4. Pull the [chart series](user-guide/chart-series.qmd) that feed Figures 1
   and 2 and the public-debt stress blocks.
5. Keep baseline and shock assumptions as separate
   [named scenarios](user-guide/scenarios.qmd).

## Using the spreadsheet instead

If you want to fill and interpret the official workbook without Python, start
with the [Spreadsheet Guide](user-guide/spreadsheet-guide.qmd). It includes a
download of the IDA21 template plus cell maps generated from the input and
output bindings.

## What this library does not do

It reproduces workbook arithmetic. It does not choose a data vintage, decide
debt coverage, design a customized scenario, or write the judgement paragraph
that sits next to a mechanical rating. Those remain economist decisions.

Workbook comparison for the shipped scenario sweep is documented on
[Excel parity validation](user-guide/excel-parity-validation.qmd).
